computed.yaml is a list under `fields:`. Each entry names a `table` and a `column` and has either `expr:` or `sql:` with `triggers:`. The column is an ordinary column declared in schema.prisma; give it a default for rows that have nothing to compute yet (`@default(0)` for a count).

`expr:` is an SQL expression over the columns of the same row (`quantity * unit_price`). It is recalculated after every insert and every update of that row. It is one expression and takes no parameter.

`sql:` is a SELECT with exactly one `?` and no other parameter. `triggers:` lists each child table that can change the result: `table`, `fk` (the child's column that holds the parent's id) and `on:` (the child writes that recalculate: insert, update, delete). `on:` is required; list all three for a count or a sum. On such a write the `?` becomes the child's `fk` value and the result is stored in the parent row whose `id` equals it.

An update of a child recalculates the parent it names and, when the key changed, the parent it left (also when the key becomes NULL). A soft delete is an update, so `AND deleted_at IS NULL` in the SQL takes soft-deleted children out of the result.

The table, the column, each trigger table and each `fk` must be in schema.prisma, and the expression may read only columns that exist; anything else is refused when the file is written (api({at:'schema'}) config_references). A framework table is refused as a field's table and as a trigger table (api({at:'schema'}) framework_tables). The nested shape `<table>: { <column>: { expr | sql, triggers } }` loads the same way.

The write gate (write_file, edit_file, `benmore push`, `benmore deploy`) and `benmore check` make the checks the app makes when it loads the file, so a file the app could not load is refused: an entry without `table` or `column`, an `expr:` or `sql:` that SQLite cannot compile, a second parameter. An `expr:` or `sql:` is one SQL expression (no `;`, balanced parentheses): text that ends the expression and goes on with statements of its own is refused, and an app does not load with it.

An entry that would never be calculated is refused as well, because its column is still left out of every create and update: neither `expr:` nor `sql:`, `sql:` without `triggers:`, or a trigger without `on:` or with an event other than insert, update and delete. A key the file does not take (`expression:` for `expr:`) and an entry with both `expr:` and `sql:` are also refused. An app that was deployed with an entry that calculates nothing keeps loading, and its log names the field at every start as `COMPUTED NOT RUNNING`.
